newsitem.title: UK: Forward tumbles after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Forward tumbles after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Forward Group Plc plummeted on Monday after the electronics group posted a sharp rise in first-half profits but warned of a squeeze on earnings in the second half of the year.
Shares in the maker of printed circuit boards were down 144p at 137-1/2 by 1420 GMT though no trading was recorded in the stock.

Pre-tax profit jumped to 6.2 million stg in the six months ended July 1996, up from 2.0 million a year before, but executive chairman Ray Chamberlain said full-year results were likely to be below market estimates.
Chamberlain said current market conditions were having an unfavourable impact on the group's second-half performance.

He said it was too early to estimate precisely the effect but warned that results for the year to January "will now fall substantially below market expectations with little contribution expected in the second half."

Today's results also showed turnover jumping to 53.5 million stg in the first half from 20.5 million a year before and earnings per share rising to 7.5p from 3.6p. The company raised its dividend to 1.0p per share from 0.8p.
At its annual general meeting in June Forward, which floated in June 1995, said the year had started well and the group was performing ahead of its budget.
